title: Every coordinate face of a finite simultaneous SNC root algebra is regular
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring such that $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, $r\geq0$, be equations of the pairwise distinct reduced irreducible branches of a strict normal crossings boundary on $X$, with these branches precisely the closed subschemes $V(t_i)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $n\geq1$ be an integer whose image $n\cdot1_A$ is a unit, and put $$C_n=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),$$ using multivariate polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then for every subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ the quotient ring $C_n/(x_j)_{j\in J}$ is a regular Noetherian ring: each of its prime localizations is a regular local ring. Equivalently, the closed subscheme $V(x_j:j\in J)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C_n$ is regular. No irreducibility or nonemptiness of the intersections $V(t_j:j\in J)$ is assumed: they may be empty or disconnected, and then the zero ring is allowed. For $J=\varnothing$ this is the regularity of $C_n$ itself; for $r=0$ one has $C_n=A$.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra on a regular SNC pair; the faces $x_j=0$ are the root algebras over the regular strata $V(t_j:j\in J)$. Branch-parameter criterion: Stacks Tag 0BIA (etale-lemma-strict-normal-crossings), literature/stacks-project/etale.tex. Same source as lem-sfb-snc-finite-root-regular-ring, whose case $J=\varnothing$ this generalizes.

proof.text:
Fix $J\subseteq I=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and write $E_J=C_n/(x_j:j\in J)$. Setting precisely these variables to zero gives an isomorphism
$$E_J\cong (A/(t_j:j\in J))[x_i:i\in I\setminus J]/(x_i^n-\bar t_i:i\in I\setminus J).$$
The forward map sends coefficients to their quotient classes, sends each killed coordinate to zero and fixes every remaining coordinate; the reverse map sends coefficients and remaining coordinates to their classes in $E_J$. The root relations for $j\in J$ impose exactly $t_j=0$, since $n>0$, and both composites fix all generators. The affine regular scheme $X$ is locally Noetherian by [def-weil-regular-scheme], so $A$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. The finite polynomial presentation makes $E_J$ Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra before invariants; explicit face and partial-root induction supplied by Q37.

proof.text: Fix a prime $q$ of $E_J$ and put $p=q\cap A$, $R=A_p$, $S=\{i\in I:t_i\in p\}$ and $d=\dim R$. The root relations give $J\subseteq S$. For every $L\subseteq S$, put $R_L=R/(t_l:l\in L)$. The scheme-theoretic intersection of these branches contains $p$; by [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] its local ring at $p$ is regular local and has dimension $d-|L|$, meaning $\dim R_L+|L|=d$. This stalk is indeed $R_L$: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies the affine stalks with prime localizations, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] identifies the localized quotient with $A_p/(t_l:l\in L)A_p$, sending every coefficient and surviving $t_i$ to its indicated image. For $L=\varnothing$ this gives $R$ regular local. If $i\notin S$, then $t_i$ is a unit in $R$ and in every $R_L$.

source.place: Tag 0BIA, lemma-strict-normal-crossings, regular-intersection criterion; the boundary definition explicitly includes the local dimension equality.

proof.text:
For every $L\subseteq S$ and $K\subseteq I\setminus L$, define
$$B_{L,K}=R_L[x_i:i\in K]/(x_i^n-t_i:i\in K).$$
We prove simultaneously for all such $L$ and $K$ that $B_{L,K}$ is regular, by induction on $|K|$. Every ring displayed is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives the free $R_L$-basis $\prod_{i\in K}x_i^{a_i}$ with $0\leq a_i<n$. The iterated one-variable presentation agrees with the displayed presentation in any order: maps fixing coefficients and taking each coordinate to its namesake are well defined on the root relations and are inverse on the generators. For $K=\varnothing$, $B_{L,K}=R_L$ is regular by step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. This proves the induction base for every $L$.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra before invariants; explicit face and partial-root induction supplied by Q37.

proof.text: Assume the induction claim for fewer than $|K|>0$ roots and choose $i\in K$. Put $K'=K\setminus\{i\}$, $D=B_{L,K'}$ and $B=D[T]/(T^n-t_i)=B_{L,K}$, with root $u$. The induction hypothesis makes $D$ regular. Let $Q$ be a prime of $B$ containing $u$. Since $t_i=u^n$, an index $i\notin S$ would make $u$ a unit, a contradiction. Thus $i\in S\setminus L$. The image of $t_i$ in $R_L$ is nonzero: otherwise $R_{L\cup\{i\}}=R_L$, contradicting the dimension equalities $\dim R_L+|L|=d$ and $\dim R_{L\cup\{i\}}+|L|+1=d$ from step 2. The regular local ring $R_L$ is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], so multiplication by $t_i$ is injective on $R_L$. It is injective on the free $R_L$-module $D$ as well, coefficient by coefficient in the monomial basis of step 3.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra before invariants; explicit face and partial-root induction supplied by Q37.

proof.text: Quotienting $D$ by $t_i$ gives $D/(t_i)\cong B_{L\cup\{i\},K'}$. Explicitly, send coefficients from $R_L$ to $R_{L\cup\{i\}}$ and fix the root coordinates; conversely send those quotient coefficients and coordinates into $D/(t_i)$. These are inverse on generators, since the relations on both sides are precisely $t_i=0$ and $x_k^n=t_k$ for $k\in K'$. This is also the coefficient-quotient compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], iterated over $K'$. By the induction hypothesis this quotient is regular: its root set has size $|K'|<|K|$. Therefore [lem-sbc-root-algebra-regular-at-root] applies with base $D$, equation $t_i$, positive exponent $n$ and prime $Q$ containing $u$. Its Noetherian hypothesis is step 3, its injective-multiplication hypothesis is step 4, and its regular-quotient hypothesis is the preceding induction application. It gives $B_Q$ regular local.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra before invariants; explicit face and partial-root induction supplied by Q37.

proof.text: For a prime $Q$ of $B$ not containing $u$, primality and $t_i=u^n$ give $t_i\notin Q$. Set $F=D[1/t_i]$. It is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring], and $F[T]$ is regular by [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base]. In $F[T]/(T^n-t_i)$ the class of $T$ is invertible, with inverse $T^{n-1}/t_i$. The image of $n$ remains a unit, since it was a unit in $A$. The derivation $\partial/\partial T$ sends $T^n-t_i$ to $nT^{n-1}$, whose image is thus a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular], the ring $F[T]/(T^n-t_i)$ is regular. It is $B[1/t_i]$, by maps fixing $D$ and the root coordinate. The prime $Q$ extends to it, and its prime localization is $B_Q$: the inverse fraction maps exist because $t_i$ is already a unit in $B_Q$. Hence $B_Q$ is regular local. Steps 5 and 6 cover every prime of the Noetherian ring $B$, proving the induction step simultaneously for every $L$.

source.place: Tag 07PF, lemma-quotient-regular, with ordinary polynomial derivative after inverting the branch equation.

proof.text: Apply the completed induction with $L=J$ and $K=I\setminus J$. The ring $B_{J,I\setminus J}$ is $(A\setminus p)^{-1}E_J$: use the presentation of step 1 and send a coefficient $a/s$ to the corresponding localized coefficient and each surviving root to its localized class; the inverse evaluates polynomials in those fractions. Both maps respect every displayed relation and are inverse on generators. Every $s\in A\setminus p$ maps outside $q$, so localization further at the prime induced by $q$ gives $(E_J)_q$, with inverse maps on fractions fixing $E_J$. The induction therefore proves $(E_J)_q$ regular local for every prime $q$. Since $E_J$ is Noetherian by step 1, it is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its affine spectrum is exactly the coordinate face in the statement, so that face is regular as well. If the intersection $V(t_j:j\in J)$ is empty, its quotient ring is zero and so is $E_J$ by step 1; it has no primes and the conclusion is vacuous. Disconnected intersections cause no change, since $q$ and $p$ were arbitrary. The cases $J=\varnothing$, $r=0$, $A=0$ and $n=1$ are included in the same presentations and induction base.
